finding.claim: MEDIUM (blind/semi-blind, unauthenticated). POST /profile/avatar fetches a user-supplied URL with axios. The only validation is a scheme prefix check (startsWith('https://')), which does not restrict the host. axios follows redirects by default, so an attacker's HTTPS server can redirect to http://169.254.169.254/ or other RFC-1918 hosts such as users.internal:8080. Direct https:// URLs to internal hosts also work. Only the byte length of the response is returned, which limits it to blind SSRF. Port and host probing and size-based inference remain possible.

trace.note: Public Express route POST /profile/avatar (no auth middleware)
Check: typeof string and startsWith('https://'). Scheme-only prefix check; no hostname allowlist and no IP/RFC-1918 blocking
axios.get(url) with default redirect following (maxRedirects defaults to 5), no re-validation of redirect targets
Response is reduced to img.data.length, which leaks size only

finding.guards_checked: Scheme check (https:// prefix) only. The SSRF skill says scheme-only checks do not close a finding. No hostname set membership, no URL parsing, no .hostname comparison, no maxRedirects:0, no CIDR or egress control in the repo, and no authentication on the route. Not closed.

verdict.guard_found: none (only a scheme-prefix check, url.startsWith("https://"), at server.js:11)
verdict.reason: server.js:10 takes req.body.avatarUrl from an unauthenticated route and server.js:14 passes it to axios.get after only the scheme-prefix check at server.js:11, with no host validation and default redirect following; server.js:15 returns only the byte length, so the SSRF is blind or semi-blind.
